question.text: Kanchenjunga Credit Fund (Cat II) has completed its original 7-year tenure and 2-year extension. No further extension has been voted. What is the maximum period within which the AIF must fully liquidate, and what is the threshold for any extension?

answer.text: Must liquidate within 3 months; no further extension permitted
Must fully liquidate within 1 YEAR following expiration of tenure (original or extended) in absence of 2/3 unit-holder consent
May extend indefinitely with Sponsor's approval
Must liquidate immediately on tenure end

explanation.text: The Logic: Tenure of Cat I/II AIFs may be extended up to 2 years with approval of two-thirds of unit-holders by value. In the absence of such consent, the AIF must fully liquidate within 1 year following expiration of the original or extended tenure. The Trap: Option A (3 months) is over-aggressive. Option C is operational overreach with no regulatory basis. Option D (immediate) ignores the orderly wind-up window. Note: Workbook page 341 states tenure extension and the 1-year liquidation timing; pages 287 and 298 provide related disclosure and dissolution-period context.
